newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria left calls for Nazi victim compensation.
newsitem.headline: Austria left calls for Nazi victim compensation.

text.p: Austria's leftist Green party on Thursday called on the government to compensate Austrians for property stolen or confiscated under Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler's regime.
"Of course the human suffering that the victims had to bear cannot be measured in figures. But the financial part is definitely calculable," Greens spokeswoman Terezija Stoisits said in a statement.
The material damage inflicted by the Nazis during their control of Austria from 1938 to 1945 was estimated at around 200 billion schillings ($18.4 billion), the Greens said.

But parliamentary president Heinz Fischer, a member of the ruling Social Democrats, said that the value of the possessions lost by those persecuted during the Nazi period could not be calculated due to a lack of data.

"Since there is a lack of concrete information and reliable data, it is not possible to undertake any estimates. Therefore, there have not been and will not be any attempts to do so," Fischer said in a written reply to an initial inquiry by the Greens.
The government believed those who suffered had been fairly compensated through a variety of ways, he added.
Stoisits said the government's reply was unsatisfactory and the Greens would demand a debate on the issue in parliament.
"It seems as if the government is biding its time and hopes that by doing so it may shirk its responsibility," she said.
Stoisits urged Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's government to at least set up a body to provide legal and social counselling and look after old and ailing victims of Nazi aggression in Austria.
"We are talking about people who were once at home here and were driven out. Let us extend our help to them a little more than we have done so far," she said.
Hitler, born in the western Austrian town of Braunau-am-Inn, was given a rousing welcome by tens of thousands of people when he drove into Vienna following the 1938 annexation of Austria.

Around 65,000 Austrian Jews were killed in the Nazi Holocaust, thousands more escaped extermination by fleeing the Alpine country. Thousands of gypsies, communists and homosexuals were also sent to death camps.
The Austrian parliament last year voted to pay out financial compensation to an estimated 30,000 Austrian victims persecuted under Nazi rule.

The vote was finally agreed after years of criticism that post-war governments, mainly made up of Socialists and conservatives, had ignored their moral duty by failing to agree compensation. West Germany set up a compensation fund shortly after the end of World War Two.
